body.statement: For sample sizes in the deterministic eventual regime \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), the sets \(\mathcal C_n(a)\) are intervals, and \(\Pr_P\{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\text{ for all }a\in J\}\to1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\). The image construction in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\) is therefore an eventual-regime simultaneous \((1-\alpha)\)-level confidence set for \(\tau_{\zeta}\) for every fixed \(\zeta\), including the empty and all-domain conventions.
body.justification: Joint LR calibration should report the scientifically interpretable crossing doses and the whole curve with one common coverage event.
body.gap: Doss (2026) reports pointwise LR intervals in the nurse-staffing application; the proposition uses a genuinely simultaneous LR critical value and a coverage-preserving inverse map.
body.consumer: The inversion map loses no coverage relative to the common LR event, but that event's nominal probability remains unproved.

obligation.what_is_open: The deterministic interval and threshold-crossing inversion is complete, but its nominal limiting coverage is exactly the unresolved probability statement in feasible calibration.
obligation.obstruction: Convexity and set-image arguments preserve coverage of the common LR event; they cannot prove that the current critical value has limiting probability \(1-\alpha\).
obligation.attempted: The constrained value function was shown convex, the band event was identified exactly with the supremum event, and the true monotone curve was mapped to its threshold crossing under all stated conventions.
obligation.partial_result:
For a fixed \(k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define
\[
L_k(t)=\min_{u\in\mathcal C_n,\,u_k=t}
\sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{(i)}-u_i)^2.
\]
The feasible set is nonempty because it contains \(t\mathbf 1\).  If \(u^{(1)}\) and \(u^{(2)}\) are feasible at \(t_1\) and \(t_2\), then, for every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\),
\[
\lambda u^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)u^{(2)}\in\mathcal C_n,
\qquad
[\lambda u^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)u^{(2)}]_k
=\lambda t_1+(1-\lambda)t_2.
\]
Convexity of squared loss and passage to infima show that \(L_k\) is convex.  Hence
\[
Q_n(a,t)=L_{k(a)}(t)-
\min_{u\in\mathcal C_n}\sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{(i)}-u_i)^2
\]
is convex in \(t\), and each sublevel set \(\mathcal C_n(a)\) is an interval, allowing the empty interval and \(\mathbb R\).  Positivity of \(\widehat\kappa\) gives the exact event identity
\[
\{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in J\}
=\left\{\sup_{a\in J}
\frac{Q_n(a,\theta(a))}{\widehat\kappa(a)}
\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\right\}
=\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
On this event, the nondecreasing curve \(\theta\) is an admissible selector in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\), so its threshold crossing \(\tau_\zeta\) belongs to the image set under the stated empty-set and endpoint conventions.  Thus inversion preserves whatever coverage the common LR event has, but it cannot establish the unresolved nominal calibration probability.
